title: No single-flight/coalescing on cache miss — concurrent requests each re-fetch, re-validate, and re-write KV + D1 (thundering herd)
reasoning: resolveTokens calls refresh() on every KV miss with no deduplication: each concurrent request that misses the cache performs its own upstream fetch (a large JSON token list, 15s timeout), its own schema/EIP-55 validation, its own KV put, and up to ~350 individual D1 upserts at concurrency 20 (writeThroughD1). Because the KV TTL expires for all requests simultaneously, a burst at expiry multiplies upstream load and D1 write statements by the request concurrency. Correctness is preserved but the cost scales linearly with concurrent misses; on a shared upstream (Uniswap list) this is exactly the stampede pattern single-flight caching exists to prevent.
recommendation: Coalesce in-flight refreshes: memoize the refresh Effect per chainId (e.g. share a single in-flight promise/Effect until it settles, then clear it), so concurrent missers await the same refresh instead of starting their own. Optionally serve the D1 snapshot immediately while refreshing in the background.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature; a test would need concurrent Effect fibers asserting a single fetch call.
suggestedRegressionTest: Run N concurrent listTokens calls against an empty KV with a counting fetcher and assert the fetcher is invoked exactly once.
minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/services/token-list.service.ts makeTokenListService (add a shared in-flight refresh handle keyed by chainId).
